primitives.meaning: an incident state change that could change what an affected party should do or expect
entryFilters: an incident state change that could change what an affected party should do or expect
no instance of this journey is already open for the the incident
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.does: Determine who is materially affected, what is known, what is not known, what action the user needs to take, any safe workaround, and the condition under which the next meaningful update would happen. Saying what is not yet known is information; leaving it out and stating the rest as certainty is not

primitives.asks: Can the affected cohort be identified with reasonable precision?

branches.label: It can
branches.test: the affected population is identifiable by account, region, capability or cohort

branches.label: It cannot yet
branches.test: the boundary of the impact is genuinely unclear

primitives.does: Scope the communication to the affected population. Telling everybody about an incident affecting one region trains the whole base to ignore incident notices, and the next one will be one that matters to them

Broaden only as far as necessary, and say explicitly that the scope is still being established. Uncertainty stated is information; uncertainty implied as precision is a claim that will have to be corrected

primitives.asks: Is what would be said actually confirmed?

branches.label: Confirmed
branches.test: every claim in it is established rather than believed

branches.label: Not confirmed
branches.test: the cause, the fix or the timing is still a hypothesis

primitives.does: Say what is known and what is not, and claim nothing about cause or resolution that has not been established. A root cause announced and then retracted costs more credibility than a slow update, and technical detail stated as fact while still uncertain is the most common source of that retraction

primitives.asks: Does this materially change the guidance the recipient already has?

branches.label: It does
branches.test: what they should do, expect or avoid has changed

branches.label: It does not, and no commitment requires an update
branches.test: nothing has changed for them since the last message

branches.label: It does not, but a commitment requires an update
branches.test: a status-page cadence, a contract or a regulatory obligation requires one regardless

primitives.does: Send nothing, and record why. Sending because time has passed produces noise, and noise is what makes the eventual resolution notice go unread by the people who were waiting for it

primitives.state: no update sent; nothing material had changed
primitives.reEntry: the next material change, or the next point a commitment requires an update, brings this back

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Raise the communication through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns the obligation, the recipient resolution, the channels, the permissions and the delivery evidence.
primitives.brief: Raise the communication through the canonical communication mechanism, which owns the obligation, the recipient resolution, the channels, the permissions and the delivery evidence. Incident communication does not build its own delivery path, and the message carries no promotional content
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.asks: Is this the resolution notice for this recipient scope?

branches.label: It is
branches.test: the incident is resolved for the population this message goes to

primitives.state: update issued; the next update is bound to a stated condition rather than to a clock
primitives.reEntry: the stated condition occurring, or a material change, produces the next update

primitives.state: resolution communicated to this recipient scope
primitives.reEntry: a relapse is communicated as a relapse rather than as a new incident, because the recipients were told it was over
